title: The Leaf Factory
subtitle: How Plants Make Food from Sunlight
description: Step inside a leaf and witness photosynthesis — the process that feeds nearly all life on Earth.

segments.label: Light Absorption
segments.description: Chlorophyll in the leaf captures sunlight energy.

segments.label: Water Splitting
segments.description: Water molecules are split using light energy, releasing oxygen.

segments.label: Carbon Fixation
segments.description: CO₂ from the air is converted into glucose molecules.

segments.label: Sugar Production
segments.description: Glucose is assembled and stored as the plant's food.

interactions.prompt: Hold to charge the chlorophyll with sunlight!
Swipe to split the water molecule!
interactions.description: Break H₂O into hydrogen and oxygen.

interactions.prompt: Sort the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis
interactions.description: Categorize molecules as inputs or outputs.
Assemble the chemical equation in order.

segments.description: Inside a chloroplast, surrounded by thylakoid discs
Inside the xylem, watching water flow up
Looking through the stomata as CO₂ enters
Following glucose as it travels through the plant

hotspots.label: Chlorophyll

hotspots.label: Water Split

assessment.instructions: Answer the following questions about photosynthesis based on what you just experienced.

levels.label: Recall & Understand
levels.description: Test your recall of key photosynthesis facts.

items.question: What pigment in plants captures sunlight for photosynthesis?
items.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy.

items.question: What gas is released as a byproduct of photosynthesis?
items.explanation: Oxygen is released when water molecules are split during the light reactions.

levels.label: Apply
levels.description: Apply your photosynthesis knowledge to new situations.

items.question: A plant is placed in a sealed jar with no light. After a week, the oxygen level in the jar has dropped. Why?
options: The plant consumed oxygen through respiration without producing more via photosynthesis
The oxygen leaked out of the jar
The plant converted oxygen back into water
items.explanation: Without light, photosynthesis cannot occur, so no new O₂ is produced. The plant still respires, consuming the existing O₂.

levels.label: Implement
levels.description: Construct and order concepts about photosynthesis.

items.question: Arrange the steps of photosynthesis in the correct order.

items_to_order.label: CO₂ is fixed into organic molecules

items.explanation: Photosynthesis proceeds: light absorption → water splitting (light reactions) → carbon fixation (Calvin cycle) → glucose production.
